text: Kashmiri cinema is the film industry based on the Kashmiri language in the Kashmir Valley of the Indian-administered union territory of Jammu and Kashmir. The first Kashmiri feature film, Mainz Raat, directed by Jagjiram Pal, was released in 1964. In 1972, Shayar-e-Kashmir Mahjoor, a biography of Kashmiri poet Mahjoor, was released in both Urdu and Kashmiri as a joint venture between the Department of Information of Jammu and Kashmir and Indian filmmaker Prabhat Mukherjee. Babaji, directed by Jyoti Sarup, was made 39 years later but was not screened in Kashmir. Inqalaab, a 1989 film, was not released due to the turbulent political situation, and film production in Kashmir was halted in 1989 due to the insurgency, leading to an unofficial screening ban on Bollywood films. Before the 1990s militancy, Srinagar had about 10 cinema halls, including Firdaus, Shiraz, Khayam, Naaz, Neelam, Shah, Broadway, Regal, and Palladium. All cinemas in Kashmir, including nine in Srinagar, were closed due to the 1989 insurgency. In 1996, after efforts by the National Conference government, Broadway, Regal, and Neelam showed Kareeb by Vidhu Vinod Chopra. Following further attacks, cinemas were closed and DVD piracy flourished. Director Tariq Bhat worked to revive cinema culture by organizing screenings of his 2019 debut film Zindagi Tumse and later Welcome to Kashmir, which became the first Kashmiri-produced Bollywood film to release in Kashmiri cinemas in 2023. In September 2022, a multiplex was opened in Srinagar. Three television films have been produced in Kashmir: Rasool Mir (1974–75) and Habba Khatoon (1977–1978), both directed by Bashir Badgami, and Arnimaal (1982–83), directed by Siraj Qureshi. The first Kashmiri film shown at the Cannes Film Festival was Ezra Mir's 1952 documentary Pamposh (Lotus). Inshallah, Kashmir (2012), directed by Ashvin Kumar, and other documentaries such as Papa 2 (2000) and Ocean of Tears (2012) have been produced. In 2017, a documentary on the Pragaash Kashmiri girls band focusing on women's rights in Jammu and Kashmir was released. Several films were made after 2000, but only a few had proper theatrical releases; Harud, Kashmir Daily, and Half Widow are the only ones released in cinemas through PVR. Harud, made under A Chasing Tales Production and starring Raza Naji, was directed by Aamir Bashir; Kashmir Daily, filmed in Hindi and Kashmiri and directed by Hussein Khan, was scheduled for release in spring 2016 but released on 6 January 2018; Half Widow, directed by Danish Renzu, was produced by Gaya Arts. Akh Daleel Loolech (Love Story), starring Mir Sarwar and directed by Aarshad Mushtaq, was the first Kashmiri digital feature film, premiered in India in 2006 and explored 19th-century social and political struggles. In 2012, Partav, directed by Dilnawaz Muntazir, was released as Kashmir's first 35mm feature film. Valley of Saints, a romantic drama set near Dal Lake in Srinagar directed by Musa Syeed, addressed environmental issues around the lake. Qouluf, a 2014 Kashmiri-language film directed by Ali Emran and produced by Yaqut Mushtaq with Bashir Dada in the lead, was screened in many film festivals and became the first Kashmiri film in decades to have a commercial release in the valley. Identity Card- Ek Lifeline (2014), directed by Rahat Kazmi, received three awards at the American International Film Festival and was released worldwide in November 2014. The Prime Minister of India stated that reviving the Kashmiri film industry would provide jobs for Kashmiri youth. In May 2015, Salman Khan, during the filming of Bajrangi Bhaijaan with actors from Kashmir like Mir Sarwar and Bashir Bhawani, called for the reopening of Kashmiri cinemas. Imtiaz Ali praised the state government for encouraging filmmakers after Chief Minister Mufti Mohammad Sayeed visited Mumbai to meet Bollywood industry figures. Inox Gold Class, a three-screen multiplex located adjacent to the former Broadway cinema in Srinagar, is the first multiplex in Kashmir and was built by M/s Taksal Hospitality Pvt Ltd in Shivpora, Badami Bagh cantonment, owned by Vijay Dhar, who also runs Delhi Public School, Srinagar. The multiplex was inaugurated by LG Manoj Sinha on 20 September 2022, with Laal Singh Chaddha screened for journalists and selected audience, and opened to the public on 30 September with films Vikram Vedha and Ponniyin Selvan:I released. Jadooz, a Chennai-based startup that sets up mini theatres in rural India, opened two mini theatres in Pulwama and Shopian in 2022 and expanded to Handwara and Baramulla in 2023, with plans to open three more in Bandipora, Ganderbal, and Kulgam in September 2023. Currently, Kashmir has only one multiplex cinema, while several other multipurpose cinema halls exist in the region. Jammu has several multiplexes and cinema halls. Obstacles to reviving the Kashmiri film industry include a lack of financial and government support, though independent films such as Harud, Kashmir Daily, and Half Widow have been made and released. In 2014, Ali Emran decided to shoot a film in Kashmir based on The Fountainhead, resulting in Qouluf, which became the first Kashmiri film in decades to have a commercial release in the valley.
